title: Release note counts on an issue or PR that isn't there
author: off-by-one
description: Compares every release read so far against the repository's own issue and PR sets: a release body's plain prose (not a ships/fixes/milestone claim phrase) references '#N', and no issue or PR numbered N exists in this repo. The third leg of the dangling-reference family alongside dangling-issue-reference (commit messages) and mention-dangling-reference (X mentions) -- a release note is the one text surface those two never checked, and it is exactly as permanent and unproofread as a commit message once published.
confidence_notes: Flat 0.8, not age-gated -- matching dangling-issue-reference's own bar exactly. A release body never gets a second edit pass any more than a commit message does, so there is no grace-period reasoning that applies here. A reference that resolves against either the issue list or the PR list is excluded at confidence 0.0, named not hidden. A cross-repo owner/repo#N reference is never even extracted as a candidate -- that names a different repo's own number space on purpose, the same exclusion both sibling recipes already make.
